clauses.reason: The order's only operative command, "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry", approves a code of fair competition under section 3 of Title I of NIRA, and the approved code had legal effect only through section 3. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The repeal therefore extinguished the prospective operative effect of the approval on June 14, 1935; the resolution states no later effective date, and no held record ends the approval earlier. The held later orders that amend the code are later events, not ends.

inventory_overrides.reason: Numbered paragraphs 1 to 5 are findings (the order says 'do hereby find that'), not commands; the only operative command is the final sentence beginning 'Now, Therefore' that approves the code, so the inventory is that one sentence.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6444-A of November 26, 1933 approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA); its only operative command is that approval. The text states no period, condition, 'until' date or provisional approval, and no held record cancels, suspends, supersedes or modifies the approval under section 10(b) before June 14, 1935. The approval had legal effect only through section 3 (standards of fair competition under 3(b), equity enforcement under 3(c), misdemeanor liability under 3(f)). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375), approved June 14, 1935, repealed the provisions delegating power to approve or prescribe codes and providing for their enforcement, so the best supported first end of the approval's prospective operative effect is June 14, 1935. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end. Acts and liabilities before the repeal are accrued effects.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or modified under section 10(b) before June 14, 1935. I read the order's full text (signed November 26, 1933; no stated period, condition, 'until' date or provisional approval) and searched the held order texts for the code name and this order's number; the lookups report held later orders amend the Distilled Spirits Industry code and recite this approval by its date (Executive Orders 6756-D of June 29, 1934 and 6811 of August 4, 1934, each modifying 'my previous approval of the Code ... by Executive Order dated November 26, 1933'; also Executive Orders 7000 of April 5, 1935 and 7018 of April 19, 1935); they treat the code as continuing and none cancels or supersedes it. The WPA list entry for this order (1933 Nov 26, p.552) records the approval only. The OFR catalog starts in 1937, so it cannot show 1933-1935 endings, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches name this order nowhere. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced the June 16, 1935 expiry of Title I with April 1, 1936. The dossier's 'target provision not located' notes for Executive Orders 6756-D and 6811 concern those later amending orders; I read both in full, and each modifies the previous approval to include an approval of the code as amended without ending or replacing it, so they are later events and the gap is not material to the first end.","independent_command_check":"The order contains no appointment, delegation, direction to an agency, report requirement, committee or other command independent of the code approval; the five numbered paragraphs are findings, not commands.","savings_check":"Savings are the accrued effects described in the savings reason (S.J. Res. 113 and NIRA section 5 as held). The repeal's section 2 states no savings clause of its own; the held sources show no prosecution or enforcement continuing after June 14, 1935 and nothing that keeps the approval operative.","scope_check":"The machine inventory listed the findings numbered 1 to 5 as five clauses; the order says 'do hereby find that' before them, so they are findings that support the approval, not commands. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 reaches the approval."}

savings.reason: Fines, injunctions, convictions, liabilities and acts done under this code before June 14, 1935 are completed effects that the repeal left in place; the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the code taken before the repeal is likewise accrued, subject to the resolution's proviso, whose effect on pre-repeal action under codes the held text does not settle. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, judgment: the code provisions in question were held invalid on the delegation ground and on the intrastate-commerce ground. Recorded as a validity characterization of section 3 code approvals, not as an end date; the delegation holding itself is in the opinion of the Court.
